note: Paths each check group of scripts/run_ci.sh depends on (Python regular expressions over repository paths). GitHub CI and the local pre-push run select groups from the same lists through scripts/quality/ci_groups.py. The lakehouse checks are four groups, lakehouse_bronze, lakehouse_silver, lakehouse_gold and lakehouse_features, listed in layers from upstream to downstream. The bronze list is the broad lakehouse list and holds the code every layer shares (the launcher, memory plan, provenance, lock, compose file, dbt project, macros and tests, and the gold checks that the silver E2E imports); the silver, gold and feature lists name only the files that belong to that layer. A file that an upstream layer's checks read although a later layer's list also matches it is named in upstream_inputs for the earliest layer that reads it (the bronze storage and provenance runners read gold macros, two gold dimension models, the bronze staging models, the silver build marker model, the saved suites, the silver columns, gold and features publication contracts and the silver quality module), and belongs to that layer, so a change to it reruns that layer and every layer downstream. Each other path is listed for the layer that reads it first, and no later layer's list may match it: a path that several layer lists match belongs to the most downstream of them, so a later layer's pattern that also matches an earlier layer's input would hide that layer (the silver suite check reads the saved suites in features/great_expectations and the gold suite folder, so those select silver, gold and features unless upstream_inputs assigns them to bronze, and the gold list excludes them). A check whose inputs no list can name completely belongs in always. A layer's changed path selects that layer and every layer downstream of it, so a bronze or shared change selects all four, a silver change selects silver, gold and features, a gold change selects gold and features and a feature check code change selects features. The features list also names the feature store's own files (the Feast repository, its scripts, schema and publication contract, and the Feast image folder), so a change to only those files runs the features group alone, except the publication contract, which the bronze ECS stage runtime cases read and which therefore selects every layer, while a gold or feature-model change runs gold and features. Feature model, test and recipe paths remain in the gold list because the gold model metadata and bridge checks read them too. The gold list also names the training target lists and their check (config/training/targets.json, scripts/training/targets.py, run_targets_e2e.py and the package marker), which read the gold control bridge, so a bridge or target list change runs that check. A path in global selects every group; a path that no group lists and that is not passive also selects every group. The launcher group (the launcher E2E suite, about 14 minutes) is selected by the files that suite imports or reads and, while a followed module that lists files carries the inventory_reads pattern "." (owner decision 1: not reviewed), by every path: config/quality/launcher_inputs.json lists them, scripts/quality/launcher_inputs.py computes the list from the suite's entry point (imports, module names, paths and folders its code names, text files it reads) and fails when the committed list differs, and scripts/quality/ci_groups.py adds the path pattern of each inventory_reads entry (\.py$, because the Docker-call guard that the suite runs parses every Python file), one prefix per folder read whole and one exact path per listed file to the group; the pattern "." is kept apart from the group lists as launcher_always, so it selects the launcher group and never classifies a path: a path that no list names still selects every group. Until the always-select modules are narrowed, the launcher group is the one exception to "a group runs only for the paths on its list": a path that only another group lists, a document or a group body file also selects it. Each group's commands are in scripts/ci/groups/<group>.sh (the launcher's too), and that file is listed in its own group's list only: an edit to it selects that group, the layers downstream of it and repository_code_checks (which matches every .sh file and runs the guard scripts/quality/ci_group_files.py), and no other group except the launcher (launcher_always, above). scripts/run_ci.sh stays in global, and so do scripts/quality/timing.sh (every group loads it), .github/workflows/ and .github/actions/; other files under .github/ (the pull request template) are documents. The privacy, secret, credential, data-file, writing, Markdown lint and documentation gates are not groups: they run in every scope. Groups in full_only run only in the full scope (the local full run); the acquisition gate keeps its own path list in the acquisition-checks hook, which the pre-push run (once, over the pushed range) and GitHub CI use. The fast source gates (Ruff, shell syntax, ShellCheck, actionlint, yamllint, Hadolint, gofmt and go vet) run unconditionally in every scope and part. Their configuration and source inventory cannot bypass a gate through path selection. SQL style runs in every full and range run (the run before a push and GitHub CI); in the staged and paths scopes it runs when a listed SQL input changes: dbt/, .sqlfluff and services/ SQL, the dbt package archive config and the SQLFluff pins and installer. Feature execution uses separate source and column parts with the feature_shards counts below. They share the lakehouse_features dependency layer, so each runs on every input of that layer and every upstream layer. The full local scope also runs repository_hooks as the same disjoint hook_groups used by the hosted matrix, excluding only the separate local_ci aggregate. The pre-push run (scripts/quality/pre_push.py) selects groups from the pushed range with these lists, as GitHub CI does, and runs the full scope instead when the range changes a path in pre_push.full_paths (the selector and its configuration, the CI scripts and group bodies, the acquisition CI entry scripts, the workflow, the setup action and the pre-commit configuration). Its steps have the deadlines in pre_push.timeout_seconds.
